## Overview

This is the **Spring PetClinic REST** application, built with **Maven**. DTOs and API interfaces are **generated from an OpenAPI spec** at build time (openapi-generator-maven-plugin 7.23.0), so `OwnerDto`, `OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerPageDto`, and the `OwnersApi`/`OwnerV2Api` interfaces do not exist as source files — they are generated into `target/` from `src/main/resources/openapi.yml`.

Important finding up front: there is **no `sharesHousehold` field** anywhere in the entity, DTO/schema, or main source. There is also **no lastName+address duplicate check** today — the only duplicate detection that exists is on **telephone**. However, the acceptance test suite (see section 7) already expects a household-duplicate rule keyed on `lastName` + `address` with a `sharesHousehold` override. So this feature must be built.

## 1. Owner entity/model

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`

`@Entity`, `@Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person`. Fields declared on `Owner`:
- `address` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Column(name="address")`)
- `city` (`@NotEmpty`)
- `telephone` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Pattern` E.164 `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`)
- `email`
- `registrationDate` (`LocalDate`, defaulted in `@PrePersist defaultRegistrationDate()`)
- `customerCode`
- `pets` (`@OneToMany`)

`lastName` (and `firstName`) live on the superclass: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java` — `@MappedSuperclass`, both `@NotEmpty`, columns `last_name`/`first_name`, plus `getInitials()`. Person extends `BaseEntity` (holds `id`/`isNew`).

There is **no `sharesHousehold` field** on Owner or Person.

## 2. Controller handling owner creation (POST)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

`@RestController`, `@RequestMapping("/api")`, implements the generated `OwnersApi`. The create method (POST maps to `/api/owners`), lines 104-124:

```java
@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
@Override
public ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto) {
    List<String> missingFields = OwnerFieldsValidator.findMissingFields(ownerFieldsDto);
    if (!missingFields.isEmpty()) {
        throw new MissingOwnerFieldsException(missingFields);
    }
    HttpHeaders headers = new HttpHeaders();
    Owner owner = ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto);
    String telephone = TelephoneNormalizer.normalize(owner.getTelephone());
    if (!this.clinicService.findOwnerByTelephone(telephone).isEmpty()) {
        throw new DuplicateTelephoneException(telephone);
    }
    owner.setTelephone(telephone);
    owner.setEmail(EmailNormalizer.normalize(owner.getEmail()));
    this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
    OwnerDto ownerDto = ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner);
    headers.setLocation(UriComponentsBuilder.newInstance()
        .path("/api/owners/{id}").buildAndExpand(owner.getId()).toUri());
    return new ResponseEntity<>(ownerDto, headers, HttpStatus.CREATED);
}

## Summary

I implemented the household-duplicate rule for owner creation: creating an owner is rejected with **409** when another owner has the same `lastName` **and** `address` (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

The logic was placed layer-by-layer, mirroring the existing telephone-duplicate feature so no class became a catch-all:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema (default `false`, not persisted), so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` exposes it.

2. **`util/TextNormalizer.java`** (new) — a small single-purpose utility that trims, collapses internal whitespace, and lower-cases a string for comparison. Lives in the neutral `util` package so the service doesn't depend on the web layer.

3. **`rest/validation/DuplicateHouseholdException.java`** (new) — a runtime exception carrying the offending last name/address, modeled on `DuplicateTelephoneException`.

4. **`ExceptionControllerAdvice`** — added a handler mapping `DuplicateHouseholdException` → 409 `CONFLICT`, mirroring the telephone handler.

5. **Repository** — added `findByLastNameIgnoreCase(String)` to the `OwnerRepository` interface and all three implementations (Spring Data JPA, JPA, JDBC) using a `LOWER(...) = LOWER(...)` query to narrow candidates.

6. **Service** — added `findOwnersInHousehold(lastName, address)` to `ClinicService`/`ClinicServiceImpl`. It narrows via the case-insensitive query, then filters by normalized `lastName` and `address` (whitespace-collapse can't be expressed portably in JPQL, so it's applied in Java via `TextNormalizer`).

7. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after the existing telephone check, and only when `sharesHousehold` isn't `true`, it throws `DuplicateHouseholdException` if a matching household exists. The controller stays thin, delegating the query to the service.

Note: since DTOs/API interfaces are code-generated from `openapi.yml` at build time, the `sharesHousehold` field takes effect via the normal Maven build (confirmed by the passing tests).
